subject: Egypt
note: Hand-curated research for a Geographica episode about the Suez Canal. Claims are cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary). The canal is drawn as an approximate route between its two ends.

claims.text: The Suez Canal is an artificial sea-level waterway in Egypt, connecting the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea through the Isthmus of Suez and dividing Africa and Asia.
The canal is 193.3 kilometres long and is a key trade route between Europe and Asia.
Construction lasted from 1859 to 1869, and it officially opened on 17 November 1869.
It reduces the journey distance from the Arabian Sea to London by approximately 8,900 km, avoiding the South Atlantic and southern Indian oceans.

port-said.note: The Mediterranean end of the canal, at Port Said.

suez-city.note: The Red Sea end of the canal, at Suez.
